facts.claim: The Culture Code: The Secrets of Highly Successful Groups, Daniel Coyle, 2018. Three skills: build safety, share vulnerability, establish purpose.

Belonging cues include physical proximity, eye contact, energy, turn-taking, and whether everyone talks to everyone; they share three qualities (energy, individualization, future orientation) and send one message: 'You are safe here.'

Alex 'Sandy' Pentland (MIT Media Lab) used a sociometer, a sensor recording signals such as eye contact, mimicry and physical closeness, during role-played negotiations (salary, vacation, benefits). He could predict each negotiation's outcome from the first five minutes of data; the interaction mattered more than the content of the talk.
Vulnerability loop (described with Harvard's Jeff Polzer): person A signals vulnerability, B detects it, B signals their own, A detects that, and a norm of trust and closeness forms.

Dave Cooper, a military team leader in the book, has teams hold an after-action review right after each mission; enlisted men lead it, no rank, no agenda, no minutes; teams replay each decision and keep asking why. Cooper says the most important words a leader can say are 'I screwed that up.'
Pixar teams 'plus' early drafts by offering solutions rather than giving 'notes'; the book lists BrainTrusts with after-action reviews as candor-building practices.
Johnson & Johnson's Credo is a 311-word document carved into a granite wall at the New Jersey headquarters and displayed at business locations.
Coyle uses the 1982 Tylenol poisoning as a case of a crisis testing culture; the company's answer was found in the 311 words of the Credo.
J&J held regular meetings with senior managers to challenge and discuss the Credo (the 'Credo Challenge', started under CEO James Burke).
Purpose is built by linking where the group is to where it wants to go, repeating a few clear signals.

rejected.claim: A senior SEAL officer told a junior: 'I made the wrong call last operation, I should have listened to you' (Coyle observing SEAL Team Six).
rejected.reason: Not verifiable; replaced by Cooper's documented after-action practice.

rejected.claim: Pixar executives said 'I may be wrong' and 'I need help' in meetings; Pixar's streak is no coincidence (as the book's claim).
J&J CEO asked 'What do our values say?'; 31 million bottles recalled; company took a big loss and returned stronger after two years.
rejected.reason: Recall count varies by source (31 vs 32 million), the quote and the recovery claim are unverified.

rejected.claim: Credo dating from 1943 and the phrase 'patients and consumers first' in the book.
rejected.reason: Not verified against the book; omitted.
